analysis:
This batch contains only CI test scripts for the threat-review scanner. No provider, coordinator or native runtime code is touched, so no threat-model asset (A-001..A-017) or boundary (TB-002..TB-011) is directly affected.

1) .github/scripts/test-threat-diagnostics.py head 186-187,196: adds a paid-call planning stub and asserts plan_calls [2,1] during multi-tier integration. This is a test-only change.

2) .github/scripts/test-threat-integration-scope.py head 6-199: adds DepthPolicyTests, which encode the scanner's model-escalation policy:
- Critical paths (crypto, attest, workflows, renamed-from-critical) go to SOL.
- Risky production paths (auth) go to OPUS.
- Support/docs/test paths stay SONNET-only unless the reviewer reports uncertainty or findings.
- Integration uncertainty yields manual_review_reasons and clean() is false, with no blanket rescan (line 139-146).

Support files named e.g. Tests/AuthTests.swift receive no filename escalation (line 89-95). This is a deliberate policy trade-off that relies on Sonnet coverage and is not a product regression.

3) .github/scripts/test-threat-model-review.py head 743,752-761:
- THREAT_REVIEW_BASE_SHA is now asserted to come only from github.event.pull_request.base.sha; the env fallback is removed. This tightens base-revision provenance.
- The review job is asserted to exclude workflow_dispatch, pr_number and review_depth inputs, reducing manual-trigger surface.
- Timeout rises 20→60 min, plus a workload call cap (default 500) and an output-token cap.

These assertions test workflow text that is not supplied in this batch. Integration should confirm that the actual workflow YAML matches them, that pull_request_target still checks out only the default-branch scanner with persist-credentials false, and that the raised timeout and call budgets are bounded as intended.

No security regression was identified in the supplied units.
